_provenance: Fictional demo data. Weather station identity and degree-day figures are invented for the Sift 'Home Energy Guardian' hackathon scenario and do not describe any real weather station or climate record.
note: Heating degree days (HDD) and cooling degree days (CDD) for the same 18 billing cycles as usage-history.json, using the same cycle boundaries. HDD/CDD are computed against a 65F base.

cycles.note: Same calendar window as the current (anomalous) cycle, one year earlier. Used as the multi-year typical/normal CDD reference for this cycle window.
Current (anomalous) cycle. Actual CDD (460) exceeds the typical/normal CDD reference (380, from cycle 2025-08) by 80 cooling degree days.

weatherAttribution.weatherSensitivityMethodology: Regression coefficient derived from correlating cycle-over-cycle CDD against usage across the prior 17 cycles in usage-history.json for this household (fixture-authored reference value for deterministic tests).
weatherAttribution.arithmeticNote: 80 excess CDD * 2.625 kWh/CDD = 210 kWh. This explains 210 of the 490 kWh anomaly gap (see current-bill.json anomaly.usageGapAboveBaselineKwh); the remaining 280 kWh is not explained by weather alone.
weatherAttribution.conclusion: Weather explains part but not all of the usage increase. The remaining 280 kWh requires household-event correlation.
